name.en: Fake government call: “your identity was used in a crime, pay at a Bitcoin ATM”

how.en: A caller says they are from the Government of Canada, the CRA, Service Canada, the RCMP or a “Crown Attorney Office”. They claim your identity was used for a crime, that you owe money, or that there is a warrant, and threaten arrest, charges or jail. To “clear your name” they tell you to withdraw cash and put it into a Bitcoin ATM, often by scanning a QR code they send on WhatsApp. They may also send emails on fake government letterhead.

text.en: A caller says they are a government official or police and that you are facing arrest or charges.
They demand immediate action and tell you to keep it secret from family and your bank.
They keep you on the phone while you go to the bank and withdraw cash.
They send a QR code on WhatsApp and tell you to deposit the cash at a Bitcoin ATM.

Government of Canada – Office of the Crown Attorney. Your Social Insurance Number has been linked to criminal activity. A warrant will be issued for your arrest unless you verify your identity today. Stay on the line with the officer and do not inform your bank.

en: told to put cash in a bitcoin atm
government official said i would be arrested
my sin was used in a crime
scan a qr code at a bitcoin machine
cra said there is a warrant for my arrest
Threats of arrest, charges, jail or deportation on the phone or by message.
Being told to pay by Bitcoin ATM, crypto, gift cards or prepaid cards.
A QR code sent by a stranger for a payment.
Being told to stay on the line or keep it from your family or bank.
Hang up. The government and police never demand payment by crypto, Bitcoin ATM or gift cards, and never threaten arrest by phone.
Don’t scan QR codes from strangers.
Check by calling the agency on a number from its official website.
If you paid, call your bank, then report it to your local police and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.
